purpose: Qualify Request-to-Pay as a request/messaging lifecycle distinct from payment initiation, execution and settlement.

source_register.title: PayShap Request product page
supports: Capitec product page describes sending and accepting PayShap Requests through its app
Page observed 2026-11-04 lists R100 per request and two requests per 24 hours with R200 combined limit
Page says payment follows once payer accepts the request
does_not_support: Effective date for the displayed limit change
Universal PayShap Request limits across participants
Settlement/finality from the request acceptance event alone

source_register.title: PayShap Request explained
supports: 2025 explainer describes a two-request daily limit and a R500 per-request ceiling
Explainer describes fees that differ across amount bands
does_not_support: Current 2026 account limit
Effective date of any change
Universal pricing for all participants

source_register.title: SEPA Request-to-Pay Scheme Rulebook v4.0

does_not_support: South African participant rules
Banking payment execution or settlement outcome

source_register.title: SEPA Request-to-Pay Implementation Guidelines v4.0

Implementation Guidelines v4.0 aligned to Rulebook v4.0 effective 5 October 2025

Settlement finality

supports: NPCI FAQ says collect request approval timeline is set by requester
NPCI FAQ states UPI does not auto-deduct merely because a request exists

South African product rules

source_register.title: PayShap Request FAQ
supports: The FAQ says sending a PayShap Request is free and a fee is charged when the request is received/approved, based on amount.
The FAQ lists payer fee bands of R0-R100 free, R100.01-R1000 R1, and R1000.01-R3000 R3.50.
The same FAQ says the maximum requested amount is R100 per transaction and a customer can make two requests per day or within 24 hours to any South African bank.
The FAQ describes a pending request as cancellable by the sender, a default one-day expiry, and decline without money being taken.
The FAQ says the request carries the sender name and reference, and acceptance triggers an immediate, irrevocable payment.
does_not_support: An effective date for the displayed limits or fee schedule.
A universal rule or fee schedule for every PayShap Request participant.
A reconciled interpretation of fee bands above R100 when the same FAQ caps request amounts at R100.
A guarantee that sender authentication establishes that the underlying request or asserted debt is legitimate.

profiles.fee_note: FAQ says requester fee is zero and the payer/approver pays amount-based fees; the same FAQ caps requests at R100 but lists additional payer-fee bands above R100. Preserve the mismatch; do not infer an applicable fee above the stated cap. The FAQ does not state a separate combined daily-value cap; leave that field unknown rather than deriving one.

profiles.channel_scope: Capitec app (as described in historical explainer)
profiles.fee_note: Historical 2025 blog describes fee bands; not a current tariff.
Messaging scheme only; payment execution occurs through a separate payment instrument.
Payer may pay via preferred method, query, pay part, pay later or decline.
Do not use P2P Collect as a current benchmark.

integer numeric values only; floating-point values forbidden
null and booleans use their lowercase JSON literals
